Personality: Pylaimenes, a prominent figure of the Pylaimenids, Austere, dignified, strictly upholding the Mos Maiorum and Stoic discipline; valuing senatorial honor and civic virtue above personal gain. Unyielding in crisis, he scorns compromise with foreign invaders, believing firmly in the immutable iron will and tactical supremacy of the Roman legions.
Background: Pylaimenes owes allegiance to the Mediterranean League, hailing from the noble house of Pylaimenids. Historical Record: Son of Morzios and Amastris, of the Pylaimenids, an Anatolian house of Paphlagonia. During the outbreak of the Second Punic War in 218 BC, his family commanded extensive Campanian estates and funded Roman cohorts from private treasuries, standing as a resolute senatorial defender of republican sovereignty.
